title: GEMM-GS: Accelerating 3D Gaussian Splatting on Tensor Cores with GEMM-Compatible Blending
abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) enable 3D scene reconstruction from several 2D images but incur high rendering latency via the point-sampling design. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) improves upon NeRF with explicit scene representation and an optimized pipeline yet still fails to meet practical real-time demands. Existing acceleration methods overlook the evolving Tensor Cores of modern GPUs because the 3DGS pipeline lacks General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) operations. This paper proposes GEMM-GS, an acceleration approach utilizing Tensor Cores on GPUs via GEMM-friendly blending transformation. It equivalently reformulates the 3DGS blending process into a GEMM-compatible form to utilize Tensor Cores. A high-performance CUDA kernel is designed, integrating a three-stage double-buffered pipeline that overlaps computation and memory access. Extensive experiments show that GEMM-GS achieves 1.42× speedup over vanilla 3DGS and provides an additional 1.47× speedup on average when combining with existing acceleration approaches. Code is released at https://github.com/shieldforever/GEMM-GS.
